title: Interleaved region-tier failover arbiter with blue-green variant arbitration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an "arbiter" routing policy that interleaves region and tier priorities when evacuating traffic from Dedicated pools to Hosted during capacity pressure or maintenance. The arbiter must perform blue-green style variant arbitration (primary/secondary model variants) while preserving KV/prefix cache locality, respecting tenant affinity, and applying tenant-weighted hysteresis to avoid thrashing. Goals: minimize tail latency regressions, limit token-cost blowup, and provide clear operational controls (circuit breakers, manual override, safe rollback).
acceptance_criteria: Arbiter can move a tenant from Dedicated->Hosted with <= 2x 95th pct latency increase for 95% of tenants during steady-state tests
Integrated blue-green variant arbitration ensures at most one variant demote per tenant during any ramp window
KV cache warmup preserved when transitioning within same region; tests show cache hit-rate drop < 15%
Can configure tenant-weighted hysteresis and per-tenant grace windows via policy API
Automated circuit breaker trips after configurable error-rate or token-cost thresholds and reroutes traffic to fallback variant
Operational runbook and rollback steps validated in staging run
tasks: Finalize arbiter policy proto and config knobs (Marcus)
Implement routing decision path in orchestrator with interleaved region-tier scoring (Eng team)
Wire blue-green variant selection and graceful demotion flow, including cold-start throttles
KV cache affinity hook: attempt prefix-preserving transitions when region invariant holds
Add metrics/traces: tenant_flow_id, arbiter_decision, variant_demote_reason, cache_hit_delta
Build e2e staging test harness with controlled pressure profiles
Author runbook, automate circuit breaker tuning, and write migration playbook

notes: Trade-off: aggressive demotion reduces cost but risks bursty cold-starts; decided to gate by tenant SLA tier and token-rate.
Fallback model variants should be quantized cheaper variants where available; fallback should never flip models more than once per grace window.
Prefer region-preserving moves if capacity exists in same region even at higher tier, to avoid cross-region cold-start penalty.
Cost accounting: track token-cost delta per-tenant during failover windows for chargeback and post-mortem.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and decision boundaries
Staging chaos tests: simulated Dedicated OOM and zone outage with 100 tenants at varied token rates
Cache-preservation regression tests measuring prefix KV hit-rate before/after transitions
Latency SLO validation: compare 95/99 pctiles pre/post failover windows
Canary rollout: start with 1% traffic, then 10%, 30%, 100% per tenant cohort with monitoring alerts
